text:
Bonding in which of the following diatomic molecule(s) become(s) stronger, on the basis of MO Theory, by removal of an electron?

(A) NO

$(B) N_{2}$

$(C) O_{2}$

$(D) C_{2}$

$(E) B_{2}$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If an electron is removed from the anti-bonding
orbital, then it will tend to increase the bond order.
The HOMO in NO and $O_{2}$ is antibonding molecular
orbital .

Hence, in NO and $O_{2}$ bond order will increase on
loss of electron.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text:
The product formed in the following reaction.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In acid, isobutylene is protonated to the tert-butyl cation:

$(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}^{+}$

The tert-butyl cation adds to a second isobutylene molecule, giving a tertiary octyl cation:

$(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}^{+}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}{}^{+}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$

A hydride ion is transferred from the tertiary $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ of isobutane to this cation, giving the alkane and regenerating the tert-butyl cation:

$(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}{}^{+}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}+(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{CH}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}+(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}^{+}$

The product is 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (isooctane), $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The number of N atoms in 681 g of $C_{7}H_{5}N_{3}O_{6}$ is x $\times$ $10^{21}$. The value of x is $(N_{A} = 6.02$ $\times$ $10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}) ($Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First, determine the molar mass of the compound C${}_{7}$H${}_{5}$N${}_{3}$O${}_{6}$:

Carbon (C): 12 g/mol, and there are 7 C atoms: $7\times 12=84\text{g/mol}$

Hydrogen (H): 1 g/mol, and there are 5 H atoms: $5\times 1=5\text{g/mol}$

Nitrogen (N): 14 g/mol, and there are 3 N atoms: $3\times 14=42\text{g/mol}$

Oxygen (O): 16 g/mol, and there are 6 O atoms: $6\times 16=96\text{g/mol}$

Calculate the total molar mass:

$\text{Molar mass of C}_{7}\text{H}_{5}\text{N}_{3}\text{O}_{6}=84+5+42+96=227\text{g/mol}$

Calculate the number of moles of C${}_{7}$H${}_{5}$N${}_{3}$O${}_{6}$ in 681 grams:

$\text{Moles of C}_{7}\text{H}_{5}\text{N}_{3}\text{O}_{6}=\frac{681\text{g}}{227\text{g/mol}}=3\text{moles}$

Each molecule of C${}_{7}$H${}_{5}$N${}_{3}$O${}_{6}$ contains 3 nitrogen atoms. Thus, in 3 moles, the total moles of nitrogen atoms is:

$\text{Moles of N atoms}=3\times 3=9\text{moles}$

Using Avogadro's number, calculate the number of nitrogen atoms:

$\text{Number of N atoms}=9\text{moles}\times 6.02\times 10^{23}\text{atoms/mole}$

$=54.18\times 10^{23}=5.418\times 10^{24}\text{N atoms}$

Convert this number to the form $x\times 10^{21}$:

$5.418\times 10^{24}=5418\times 10^{21}$

Thus, the value of $x$ is:

$x=5418$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text: 1 L aqueous solution of $H_{2}SO_{4}$ contains 0.02 m mol $H_{2}SO_{4}. 50$% of this solution is diluted with deionized water to give 1 L solution (A). In solution (A), 0.01 m mol of $H_{2}SO_{4}$ are added. Total m mols of $H_{2}SO_{4}$ in the final solution is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{3} m$ mols.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Half of the original solution contains $\dfrac{0.02}{2}=0.01\text{mmol}$ of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$; diluting it to $1\text{L}$ does not change this amount, so solution (A) contains $0.01\text{mmol}$.

After $0.01\text{mmol}$ more is added, the final solution contains $0.01+0.01=0.02\text{mmol}$ of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$.

In the required form, $0.02\text{mmol}=2\times 10^{-5}\times 10^{3}\text{mmol}$, so the blank is $2\times 10^{-5}$, which is 0 to the nearest integer.

Hence, the answer is 0.

text:
For a given chemical reaction

$γ_{1}$A + $γ_{2}$B $\to$ $γ_{3}$C + $γ_{4}$D

Concentration of C changes from 10 mmol $dm^{-3}$ to 20 mmol $dm^{-3}$ in 10 seconds. Rate of appearance of D is 1.5 times the rate of disappearance of B which is twice the rate of disappearance A. The rate of appearance of D has been experimentally determined to be 9 mmol $dm^{-3} s^{-1}$. Therefore, the rate of reaction is $_____________$ mmol $dm^{-3} s^{-1}. ($Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Rate $=\frac{1}{r_{1}}\left (\frac{-d[A]}{dt}\right )=\frac{1}{r_{2}}\left (\frac{-d[B]}{dt}\right )=\frac{1}{r_{3}}\left (\frac{d[C]}{dt}\right )$

$=\frac{1}{r_{4}}\left (\frac{d[D]}{dt}\right )$

$\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{D}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_{4}}{\mathrm{r}_{2}}\left (\frac{-\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{B}]}{\mathrm{dt}}\right )$

$\frac{r_{4}}{r_{2}}=\frac{3}{2}$

$\frac{-\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{B}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{1}}\left (\frac{-\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{A}]}{\mathrm{dt}}\right )\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{r}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{1}}=2$

$r_{2}=2r_{1}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{r}_{4}=1.5\mathrm{r}_{2}=3\mathrm{r}_{1} \\  \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{C}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=1\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{mol}\mathrm{dm}^{-3}\sec ^{-1} \\  \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{D}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=9\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{mol}\mathrm{dm}^{-3}\sec ^{-1} \\  \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{D}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{r}_{4}}{r_{3}}\cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{C}]}{\mathrm{dt}}\Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{r}_{4}}{\mathrm{r}_{3}}=9 \\  \\ \mathrm{r}_{4}=9\mathrm{r}_{3}=3\mathrm{r}_{1} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}_{1}=3\mathrm{r}_{3} \\  \\ \begin{array}{l} 3\mathrm{r}_{3}\mathrm{A}+6\mathrm{r}_{3}\mathrm{B}\to \mathrm{r}_{3}\mathrm{C}+9\mathrm{r}_{3}\mathrm{D} \end{array} \\  \\ \begin{array}{ll} \therefore \text{rate of reaction} & =\dfrac{1}{9}\times 9\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{mol}\mathrm{dm}^{-3}\sec ^{-1} \\  \\ =1\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{mol}\mathrm{dm}^{-3}\sec ^{-1} \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text:
If [$Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}$]$^{2+}$ absorbs a light of wavelength 600 nm for d-d transition, then the value of octahedral crystal field splitting energy for [$Cu(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$^{2+}$ will be $____________$ $\times$ $10^{-21} J$. [Nearest Integer]

(Given : h = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$ and c = 3.08 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{4}]^{2+}$ is tetrahedral

$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ is octahedral

$\because \Delta _{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{4}{9}\times \Delta _{0}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta _{\mathrm{t}}=\dfrac{6.63\times 10^{-34}\times 3.08\times 10^{8}}{600\times 10^{-9}} \\  \\ \Delta _{0}=\dfrac{9}{4}\times \dfrac{6.63\times 10^{-34}\times 3.08\times 10^{8}}{600\times 10^{-9}}\approx 765.7\times 10^{-21}\mathrm{J} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift

text: Number of grams of bromine that will completely react with 5.0 g of pent-1-ene is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-2} g. ($Atomic mass of Br = 80 g/mol) [Nearest Integer]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Molar mass of $C_{5}H_{10} = 12$ $\times$ 5 + 10 = 70 gm

Given mass of $C_{5}H_{10} = 5 gm$

$\therefore$ Moles of $C_{5}H_{10} =$ $\frac{5}{70}$

From reaction,

1 mole of $C_{5}H_{10}$ reacts with 1 mole of $Br_{2}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{5}{70}$ moles of $C_{5}H_{10}$ reacts with $\frac{5}{70}$ moles of $Br_{2}$

$\therefore$ Reacted $Br_{2} =$ $\frac{5}{70}$ $\times$ 160 gm

= 11.428 gm

= 1142.8 $\times$ $10^{-2} gm$

$\simeq$ 1143 $\times$ $10^{-2} gm$
